claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure composed of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and exhibits tensile brittleness.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries cause local stress concentrations and contribute to the alloy's room-temperature brittleness.
Light cold rolling by approximately 10–15% thickness reduction followed by annealing at 500–600°C for several minutes is the proposed intervention.
The proposed treatment will modify the internal interfaces of the dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The proposed treatment will slightly refine the lamellar spacing.
The modified interfaces will become more coherent.
The modified interfaces will be better able to absorb or deflect dislocations.
Controlled cold deformation will introduce a relatively uniform dislocation substructure.
Low-temperature annealing after deformation will promote partial recovery at interlamellar boundaries.
Partial recovery will enhance the ability of interlamellar interfaces to act as dislocation sinks.
Enhanced dislocation absorption at interfaces will reduce pile-ups and their associated local stress concentrations.
The modified microstructure will produce more homogeneous plastic deformation.
More homogeneous plastic deformation will mitigate local overload and microcracking during straining.
Retaining fine-scale microstructural features will preserve their strengthening contribution.
The treatment will significantly increase room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will maintain or possibly increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The predicted benefit is intended to apply under room-temperature, quasi-static tensile loading in air.
Excessive annealing may cause grain coarsening and compromise the fine-scale reinforcing microstructure.
The magnitude of ductility improvement and strength retention depends on the cold-work and annealing processing window.
